newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Sharon suggests railway to link Gaza, West Bank.
newsitem.headline: Sharon suggests railway to link Gaza, West Bank.

text.p: Israeli cabinet member Ariel Sharon proposed on Monday building a railway line through Israel that would link the Palestinian-ruled West Bank with the Gaza Strip.
Sharon, minister of national infrastructure, said tracks already existed along parts of the route and both Israel and the Palestinians would have to invest in completing the line.
"There's no reason why they can't travel in trains from Gaza to Qalqilya and Tulkarm on existing train tracks," Sharon told Israel Radio.
"I proposed connecting Gaza on existing lines while adding tracks from Kiryat Gat to the Tarkumia area to hook up to Judea (the southern West Bank)," he said.

Sharon's spokesman Raanan Gissin said hundreds of tonnes of goods were transported back and forth in trucks between the West Bank and Gaza daily and a railway would alleviate the congestion on roads in Israel linking the two areas.
Gissin said Israel would discuss the idea with the Palestinians in future talks.
He said the railway was not supposed to replace the "safe passage" route which Israel has agreed under self-rule deals to provide Palestinians wishing to travel between the West Bank and Gaza.

Most Palestinians have been barred from travelling between the two self-rule areas since Israel closed off the West Bank and Gaza Strip during a spate of Islamic suicide bombings in February and March that killed 59 people in the Jewish state.
